intro: Lesson 20: Umar's justice and care for people. To understand how Umar showed justice and care for the people he led

questions.a: He judged rich and poor equally, checked his governors, and took complaints seriously.
questions.model: Point: Umar treated people equally. Evidence: he checked governors and judged rich and poor the same. Explain: no one was above the law. Link: Allah commands justice (4:58).

questions.q: What did Umar do at night?
questions.a: Walked the streets to check on people
options: Walked the streets to check on people

questions.q: Write a newspaper-style report (no pictures of people) in the portal response box: 'The caliph who checked on his people'. Include two examples and one ayah. Start: 'In Madinah, people say their caliph ...'
questions.a: Two examples of care and justice; 4:58 or 16:90 quoted correctly
questions.model: Teacher writes the headline and first line: 'In Madinah, people say their caliph walks the streets at night to see who needs help.'

questions.q: why should a leader accept complaints?
questions.a: So he can fix injustice and stay accountable.

questions.q: how can a school prefect act like Umar?
questions.a: Treat everyone equally, listen, help those who struggle.

questions.q: A just leader treats rich and poor ...
Back to our ponder: should a leader check for himself?
questions.a: Yes: Umar did, so he could help and be fair.
